title: Tamsin and the Choir Revisited
premise: Seven years after the Sundering Edict outlawed magic and executed the last choir of oath-bound speakers, Juniper Vasquez survives by selling harmless charms in the gray city of Vell. When the old gods abruptly begin answering prayers again — wild, desperate, and wrong — Juniper's dormant swordspeaker oath ignites, marking them as both herald and heretic. Hunted by the Inquisitor Sable Wren (their former choir-sister) and guided by a fading god called the Tamsin, Juniper must gather the scattered fragments of the broken covenant before the realms collapse into silence forever. The price of survival becomes literal: reforging the covenant demands an oath-bound life freely given, and in the end Juniper speaks their own name into the new covenant — surviving not as a person, but as the living word that keeps magic lawful and the gods listening.
about_author: Zephyrine Sterling is the pen name of a former cathedral archivist who spent a decade cataloguing suppressed liturgies before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about oaths, music, and the people history refuses to remember.

chapters.title: Charms for a Godless City
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. We meet them selling luck-knots and mildew-charms in Vell's night market, hiding the scar where their oath-brand was cut away. A child's prayer at their stall is answered — impossibly — by a voice of bells. Emotional beat: weary caution cracking into terror and longing.

chapters.title: The Bells Answer
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. The answered prayer spreads; shrines across Vell ignite with uncontrolled divine attention. Juniper's severed oath-brand burns back to life on their skin. They flee the market as Inquisitors arrive. Emotional beat: panic, and the first pull of a duty they thought buried.

chapters.title: Sable Wren Comes at Dawn
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. The Inquisitor and former choir-sister arrives to investigate the miracles, carrying the execution ledger with Juniper's name still uncrossed. She recognizes the brand-scar on a captured charm-seller and hesitates one heartbeat too long. Emotional beat: loyalty straining against duty.

chapters.title: What the Tamsin Wants
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. A dying god calling itself the Tamsin manifests in a flooded chapel and reveals the truth: the covenant between realms was shattered deliberately seven years ago, and the gods' return is a symptom of its decay. It asks Juniper to reforge it. Emotional beat: reluctant acceptance of purpose.

chapters.title: Seven Years of Silence
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, Juniper's POV. We see the night of the Sundering Edict: the choir's execution, how Juniper survived by renouncing their oath aloud while their fellows sang. Emotional beat: shame revealed — survival bought with betrayal.

chapters.title: The First Fragment
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Guided by the Tamsin, Juniper retrieves the first covenant fragment from a bone-orchard outside the walls, fighting a hollowed god-corpse with a sword that speaks only when spoken to. Emotional beat: the old power waking, exhilarating and frightening.

chapters.title: Wanted: Speaker of Swords
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Vell erupts with wanted posters; Sable is ordered to hunt Juniper personally. Meanwhile Juniper finds shelter with an underground congregation of hidden believers. Emotional beat: the city becoming hostile, found-friendship offering fragile warmth.

chapters.title: The Congregation of Small Gods
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. The underground faithful — hearth-gods, door-gods, forgotten saints — offer aid but demand a promise Juniper isn't sure they can keep: that magic will be lawful again, not merely free. Emotional beat: the weight of representing everyone.

chapters.title: Sable's Ledger
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable traces Juniper through the congregations, burning shrines as she goes, but keeps crossing names out of her ledger instead of writing them in. Her superiors notice. Emotional beat: quiet rebellion hardening into open doubt.

chapters.title: The Second Fragment and the Price Named
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. The second fragment lies beneath the Inquisition's own cathedral. Stealing it, Juniper learns the covenant's final clause: it must be sealed with an oath-bound life, freely given. Emotional beat: dread — the quest now has a known cost.

chapters.title: Confrontation in the Reliquary
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Sable catches Juniper in the reliquary. Blades drawn, oaths colliding, they fight — until Sable sees the third fragment's location written in Juniper's blood. She lets them go and burns her own ledger page. Emotional beat: loyalty choosing truth over orders.

chapters.title: Where the Choir Sang Last
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. The third fragment rests at the execution ground where the choir died. Juniper returns and faces the ghosts of their fellows, who do not forgive but do teach. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: The Realms Grow Thin
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Across the land, prayers go unanswered mid-word; small gods gutter out; the sky over Vell shows the other realm like a bruise. Time is visibly running out. Emotional beat: escalating cosmic stakes made intimate and local.

chapters.title: Sable Stands Trial
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Accused of heresy-by-mercy, Sable is interrogated by High Inquisitor Corvane, who reveals he helped shatter the covenant — order itself was his god. She escapes rather than recant. Emotional beat: conversion from enforcer to witness.

chapters.title: An Alliance of Oathbreakers
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Juniper and Sable reunite as uneasy allies, trading truths: what Juniper did to survive, what Sable did to obey. The Tamsin fades further with each mile. Emotional beat: forgiveness offered without being asked for.

chapters.title: Corvane's Counter-Covenant
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV. The High Inquisitor moves to seal his own counterfeit covenant with a mass sacrifice of the underground congregation, binding magic to the state forever. Emotional beat: chilling conviction — the antagonist who believes he is saving the world.

chapters.title: Raid on the Gray Cathedral
chapters.summary: Juniper and Sable's POV. They assault Corvane's ceremony to free the captives; the fourth and final fragment is revealed to be embedded in the cathedral's altar-stone, taken from the original choir. Emotional beat: desperate, costly victory — Sable gravely wounded.

chapters.title: The Fourth Fragment
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. With Sable bleeding out beside them, Juniper draws the fragment from the altar and learns the truth of the Sundering: the choir chose to break the covenant themselves, to stop Corvane's first attempt at ownership. Their executions were mercy. Emotional beat: everything Juniper believed about their own betrayal inverted.

chapters.title: What Survival Is For
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. At the threshold between realms, the Tamsin spends its last strength holding the door open. Juniper finally understands why they alone survived: someone had to carry the whole oath out of the fire. Emotional beat: acceptance — the price named, and chosen.

chapters.title: The Reforging
chapters.summary: Climax, dual POV. As Corvane's forces breach the threshold, Juniper speaks the covenant whole — every fragment, every name, every debt — and offers their own oath-bound life to seal it. Sable answers the sword when it calls her name, sharing the burden. The covenant takes both, and holds. Emotional beat: sacrifice transformed into shared vow.

chapters.title: A City That Hears Again
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Magic is lawful; shrines stand openly; the small gods return to their doorways and hearths. Sable, half-sworn into the covenant herself, rebuilds the choir on new terms — consent, not conscription. Emotional beat: mourning braided with hope.

chapters.title: Tamsin and the Choir Revisited
chapters.summary: Juniper's coda-POV, somewhere between realms. Juniper exists now as the covenant's living word — heard in every honest oath, present whenever two people make a promise and mean it. In Vell, a child prays at a charm-stall and is answered gently. Emotional beat: transcendence — survival redefined as becoming the thing that lets others live.
